speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have persistent vomiting and chest pain; to start our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and does the pain radiate to your jaw, arm, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture).

The combination of forceful vomiting, a preceding episode of retching, sudden onset of severe chest pain, and coughing strongly suggests a perforation of the esophagus. I will need to confirm this with imaging immediately.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay (upright and decubitus views).
REQUEST TEST: Serum amylase and lipase levels.
